content.value: Artificial crafting is a two-station process that trades one Artificial Tome for a choice between compatible high-tier affixes. It works only on Rare, non-Unique equipment and the item may have only one unrevealed or revealed Artificial rune at a time.
Its shaped recipe is Amethyst Shard, Ender Eye, Amethyst Shard across the top; three End Stone across the middle; and three Obsidian across the bottom.

Put the Rare item and an Artificial Tome into the Runic Altar.
Press the altar button. If both prefix and suffix space are available, the altar chooses a side randomly. If only one side has space, it uses that side.
If all three prefixes and all three suffixes are occupied, the altar randomly chooses a side and removes one random rune from that side.
The result receives an unrevealed Artificial marker reserving the chosen affix side. Take this item to an Artificial Altar.

Place the marked item into the Artificial Altar. No second tome or material is required.
The altar builds up to three options of the reserved prefix or suffix type. Options must match the equipment and armour affinity, have positive selection weight, and not duplicate a group already on the item or another displayed option.
Each option independently receives a random T1, T2, or T3 tier and its numeric value is rolled immediately.
Select one displayed option. That exact stored tier and value are revealed on the item as an Artificial rune.

The three choices, tiers, and values are stored on the item, so removing and reinserting it does not reroll them. After selection, the Artificial rune occupies a normal affix slot and can be affected by later Divine, Chaos, or Annulment crafting. If it is removed, the item no longer counts as having a revealed Artificial rune.

Applying the Artificial Tome to a completely full Rare item always sacrifices one existing rune before you see the three choices. If fewer than three legal nonduplicate groups exist, the altar can show fewer than three usable options.
